name: manual_ed9964
claim: When a user's instructions contain internally contradictory values (e.g. two different version-number formats for the same bump, or an ambiguous repo-location instruction), investigate the live/factual state first (check if referenced repos/branches actually exist, what state they're in) and THEN present AskUserQuestion with options grounded in those facts -- never guess a resolution or silently pick the 'most likely' reading.

decisions.notes: User's request said 'Bump version to 1.5.0.0' (invalid 4-part semver) in one line and 'release v1.5' in another, both a downgrade from the actual current 2.0.0, plus an ambiguous 'close out using the new oramasys repos' with no repo URL given. Checking GitHub first (oramasys/Claude-Desktop-LLM already existed as a fork, its main already fast-forwarded) turned a vague question into a sharp, well-grounded 4-question AskUserQuestion set the user could answer precisely and quickly.
